title: NY State Assembly · District 32
area: Southeast Queens, including Jamaica, South Jamaica, Rochdale Village, St. Albans, Locust Manor, and parts of Richmond Hill and South Ozone Park

context.text: Longtime incumbent Vivian Cook (in office since 1991) is not seeking re-election, leaving District 32 an open seat.

Nathaniel Hezekiah III won a five-way June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 51.9% of the vote over Latoya LeGrand, Mohammed Molla, Tunisia Morrison, and Queen Johnson. LeGrand had also won the Working Families Party primary but withdrew from that general-election line.

candidates.name: Nathaniel Hezekiah III
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 51.9% of the vote in a five-candidate field

summary.text: Nathaniel Hezekiah III is a Southeast Queens community advocate and former Deputy Chief of Staff to U.S. Representative Gregory Meeks, running for the open Assembly District 32 seat after winning a five-way Democratic primary.

background.text: Hezekiah was born and raised in South Jamaica, Queens, and states he has "spent more than twenty years serving Southeast Queens."
background.quote: spent more than twenty years serving Southeast Queens

background.text: He attended P.S. 160 and New Preparatory Middle School, then Benjamin N. Cardozo High School's law program.
He holds two bachelor's degrees in business and finance, earned at St. John's University and Pennsylvania State University.
He worked with Amalgamated Transit Union Local 1056 and later served as Deputy Chief of Staff to Congressman Gregory Meeks, a role he held for nearly two decades of constituent-service work.

priorities.text: Hezekiah's campaign slogan frames his candidacy around a record of service: "When It Mattered. Nathaniel Was There."
priorities.quote: When It Mattered. Nathaniel Was There.

priorities.text: He cites accomplishments including directing more than $100,000 in scholarship funding for local students, helping recover more than $13 million owed to the Rochdale Village community, and supporting minority- and women-owned business participation in the JFK Airport redevelopment.

His platform lists housing and homeownership assistance, protecting Mitchell-Lama communities, economic development, transportation equity, a "cradle-to-career" education pipeline, protecting the social safety net, and public safety as priorities.
He states his overall commitment is "strengthening opportunity, protecting affordability, and making sure government works for the people it serves."
priorities.quote: Nathaniel is committed to strengthening opportunity, protecting affordability, and making sure government works for the people it serves.

positions.summary: Campaigns on expanding paths to homeownership and homeownership assistance for district residents.
Lists protecting Mitchell-Lama affordable-housing communities as a campaign priority.

summary.text: Paul Nichols is running on the minor-party "The Answer Party" line for Assembly District 32; he previously ran for the seat in 2022. He has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and no campaign website or public policy statements were found.

sources.title: Nathaniel Hezekiah III for New York State Assembly

researchNotes: This is an open seat: longtime incumbent Vivian Cook is not seeking re-election. Neither candidate holds current or prior elected office, so there is no official voting/sponsorship record to cite for either. No campaign website, news coverage, or Candidate Connection survey was found for Paul Nichols beyond his Ballotpedia listing; his entry is marked minimal accordingly.
